doc.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Tom Scott's New York Connection and Steve Gadd
summary: They sort out Tom Scott's album drummer as Steve Gadd and talk about his Grammy and hi-hat lick.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Tom Scott did an album there, it was the LA Express of course. They did the Joni Mitchell stuff. But then he went to New York and did one called the New York Connection with all those guys.
Well I don’t know if it was Pretty Purdie, or it may have been Steve Gadd. That’s who it was. That was the drummer.
Who finally won a Grammy by the way.

We used to call him Bad Steve Gadd. Because he had this lick with the hi-hat that was like impossible. I mean it was like 16th, 32nd notes, I mean it was this crazy thing he could do with his left hand on the hi-hat. Bad Steve Gadd. I’m sure he’s still bad too.
